questions.q: What are the two questions, in order, that drive Salesforce's Pattern Selection Guide decision tree?
options: Is it HTTP or SOAP; is it inbound or outbound?
Is this about a process or about data; does it need to happen synchronously or asynchronously?
Is it a Platform Event or Change Data Capture; is it a trigger or a Flow?
Does it use a Named Credential; does it exceed 100 callouts?
questions.explain: The decision tree first asks whether the integration is about a process/action or about data syncing, then whether it needs to be synchronous or asynchronous.

questions.q: According to the decision tree, which pattern fits a "process + synchronous" requirement?
options: Batch Data Synchronization
Request-Reply
UI Update Based on Data Changes
Remote Call-In
questions.explain: A process-oriented requirement that needs to happen synchronously — the caller waiting for an answer — maps to Request-Reply.

questions.q: Why does this lesson argue "process vs data" should be asked before "sync vs async"?
options: Because sync vs async alone doesn't distinguish Request-Reply from UI Update Based on Data Changes, both of which can involve asynchronous elements
Because Salesforce enforces this literal order in the Setup wizard
Because asynchronous integrations are always data-oriented
Because process-oriented requirements are always synchronous
questions.explain: Asking process-vs-data first cuts the decision space more cleanly, since sync-vs-async alone can't separate an action-oriented requirement from a data-syncing one.

questions.q: In the worked example (a customer's e-commerce address update should reflect in Salesforce's Contact within a few minutes), which pattern does the lesson conclude fits best?
options: Request-Reply, since the user is waiting
Batch Data Synchronization (or inbound Platform Event publishing, since the timing tolerance is loose)
Remote Call-In, since no external system is involved
UI Update Based on Data Changes, since a screen is updating
questions.explain: The requirement is about data syncing, tolerant of a short delay, and not specifically about a live UI — making Batch Data Synchronization (or an event-driven inbound alternative) the fit.

questions.q: What does this lesson recommend doing when a requirement genuinely straddles two patterns?
options: Always default to Request-Reply, since it is the most reliable pattern
Go back to the stakeholder and ask the specific clarifying question that resolves the ambiguity, rather than forcing a single label
Implement both patterns simultaneously regardless of cost
Discard the requirement as unimplementable
questions.explain: The framework's real value is generating the sharp clarifying question needed to resolve ambiguity, not guaranteeing one unambiguous answer every time.
